text:
Matty Beniers keeps finding the big goal for a Seattle team that's living on them. His overtime winner against Calgary this week was the third of his career, as Kraken contributor Alison Lukan noted, and he has eight points in 15 games, roughly his usual pace. His ice time is up over the last ten games, close to 18 and a half minutes, as Seattle leans on him.

The problem is what happens at 5v5. The Kraken have just 44.6% of the chances with Beniers on the ice, and while that is close to the team's level without him, it isn't the profile of a top center driving play. His results are being kept afloat by finishing: four goals on 15 shots, a 27% rate that can't last, and his teammates have scored 5.4 goals more than their chances deserve with him out there. Evolving-Hockey saw the same thing last season, with results running ahead of chances. He does draw penalties at a useful rate. Our projection has him around 48 points. Watch his shot count; 15 in 15 games is low for a top-six center.
headline: Beniers delivers the big goals, on borrowed luck
